purpose: Audit final diagnostic examples that both D258/D262 and D260 fail, so the next supervision target is more precise than another broad label batch.
findings: 1/4 both-fail examples prefer unsupported expansions over short supported answers.
4/4 selected unsupported candidates already carry existing judge unsupported-claim evidence, so this can be used without new labels.
1/4 failures are same-citation or citation-count-indistinguishable cases, so citation volume is not the missing signal.
The next zero-cost target should mine non-final contrasts where answer text/citation surface is close but claim scope differs.

proposed_next_supervision.name: minimal_supported_span_vs_overexpanded_answer_contrasts
proposed_next_supervision.required_positive_pattern: short/exact cited answer or abstention that avoids unsupported predicate, list, or task-scope expansion
proposed_next_supervision.required_negative_pattern: candidate with same citation surface but an unsupported predicate, dataset/list expansion, role/scope phrase, or numeric-purpose overclaim

decision.next_step: Build a zero-cost minimal-span/overexpansion contrast packet from existing non-final judged Qwen pools, then test a selector that explicitly rewards exact supported spans and penalizes unsupported judge claims.
decision.reason: The remaining failures are not missing citations or insufficient generation; they are answer-form overexpansion failures where supported short spans lose to unsupported but plausible expansions.

llm_budget.note: This target audit reads existing diagnostic artifacts only.
